intro.title: Image Lazy Loading
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a Vue app that implements image lazy loading to improve page performance. You'll learn how to delay loading images until they are about to enter the viewport, reducing initial page load time. The core concept involves using the Intersection Observer API to detect when an image becomes visible. You'll work with Vue's ref, reactive state, and lifecycle hooks to manage the loading behavior. By the end, you'll have a functional image gallery that loads images efficiently as the user scrolls.
intro.usecase: Lazy loading images is essential for performance optimization in content-heavy applications like e-commerce sites, social media feeds, and news portals. When users scroll through product galleries on Amazon or browse their Instagram feed, images load only as they enter the viewport, reducing initial page weight and improving load times. Developers implement this pattern in dashboards with data visualizations, portfolio websites with large media galleries, and any interface where numerous images would otherwise slow down the user experience.
